3. Let N be a positive integer such that the length of each interval in the partition of [a, b] into N equal subintervals is less than 1/M.

5. Define a function g(x) = \sum_{i=1}^N f_i \chi_{[x_i, x_{i+1})}(x), where \chi_{[x_i, x_{i+1})}(x) is the characteristic function of the subinterval [x_i, x_{i+1}).
6. Note that g(x) is a step function, and it is equal to f(x) for all x in [a, b].
7. Since g(x) is a step function, it is Riemann Integrable.
8. Since f(x) = g(x) for all x in [a, b], we conclude that f(x) is also Riemann Integrable.

Therefore, we have shown that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable if and only if it is bounded and has at most a countable number of discontinuities.
